sections.html:
Inver Grove Heights is a Dakota County city of 36,873 people covering about 27.9 square miles. It lies roughly nine miles southeast of Saint Paul, with Newport and Saint Paul Park across the Mississippi River. Interstate 494, U.S. 52 and Minnesota Highways 55 and 3 are the main roads.

Of all housing units, 76.9 percent are lived in by their owners, and the middle value is $363,400. With 17.9 percent of residents at 65 or older, sellers often turn out to be empty-nesters trimming down or families winding up an estate. The city has 15,158 households of 2.35 people each, rent is $1,465 at the median, household income is $101,316 and the commute averages 22.3 minutes.

sections.h2: Ways to sell an Inver Grove Heights house
sections.html:
• Agent listing: works well for an updated house, including in school areas buyers ask for such as Simley High School's attendance area, but expect showings, inspection requests and a wait for the buyer's loan.
  • Sale by owner: saves you the commission, while the disclosures, contract and negotiation are yours.
  • Cash buyer: purchases without repairs or cleaning, a fit for estate houses, rentals with tenants and homes that have put-off maintenance.

On any route, arrange the final water read, deed tax and county clearance steps early, and the closing date is far likelier to hold.

Inver Grove Heights changed its short-term rental rules effective April 1, 2025. If the owner does not live there, the minimum rental stay is 30 days, Airbnb and Vrbo listings included. Shorter stays are allowed only when the home is owner-occupied.

Long-term rentals need a city rental license. The city has been revising the license term, renewal deadline and manager rules, so the clerk is the person to ask about current terms when you sell a rented house. A buyer who will keep renting wants the license history, so collect it first.

sections.h2: City code rules that can slow a sale
sections.html:
The code enforcement office publishes the rules most often cited on residential lots, and a pre-listing walk-around helps.

Common Inver Grove Heights yard and parking rules
SubjectRule
GrassUnder eight inches, and no brush piles
FencesPermit first; 48 inch limit in the front yard, seven feet on the sides and back
Vehicles stored outsideCurrent tabs and in running order; inoperable vehicles belong in a garage
Roll-off dumpstersNot in the street; three months out of twelve on a lot unless extended
Street parkingBanned 3:00 to 6:00 AM from November 1 to April 1

Home businesses must run entirely inside the dwelling with no visible signs, which matters if the house doubles as a workshop. Violations are reported through the city's RequestTracker, and the Code Compliance Division answers questions at 651-450-2491.

sections.h2: Which school district is my house in?
sections.html: Inver Grove Heights Community Schools, Independent School District 199, serves most of the city. The western part is in District 196 (Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan), and a small northwest piece is in District 197. Put the right district in your listing, because parents search by it.

Call Utility Billing at 651-450-2520 well ahead of your move. The city asks for at least one week of notice to arrange a meter reading, and sellers should set the final read the same way so the last bill matches your closing date.

sections.h2: Deed, taxes and special steps in Dakota County
sections.html:
The deed is recorded by Dakota County Property Taxation and Records, and the state's deed tax rate is 0.0033 of the net price. The county's selling-property page flags extra steps for manufactured homes, for properties with wells or septic systems, and for owners on Medical Assistance, who may need a certificate of clearance from the county at 651-554-6555. A call before you take an offer keeps that paperwork from delaying closing.

Value challenges go through the county's open book meetings and the board of appeal in spring and early summer. Once those close, a challenge has to wait for the next year's cycle.

A property whose sewage goes somewhere other than a permitted facility needs a written septic disclosure ahead of the signed purchase agreement. Staying quiet about a system you knew of can leave you owing the buyer what it costs to bring it up to code (Minnesota Statutes 115.55, subdivision 6). On city sewer, one plain sentence covers it.

Heirs often sell here. Before anyone signs a deed, ask a title company which court papers prove who may sell. Collect the death certificate, the will if one exists, and the newest tax statement. Go room by room and sort what stays from what goes, because a cash buyer will take it with contents if you ask, and a retail buyer will expect it empty. Tell the buyer about known leaks, old repairs and any outbuildings, since the disclosure duty applies to heirs who know of problems.

sections.h2: Working through a sale step by step
sections.html: First, the money: ask an agent and a cash buyer for written estimates and compare what each leaves you after commissions, repairs and carrying costs. Then clear the small items that cause delays. Reserve the meter reading, request a tax payoff figure from the county, and check the code enforcement rules above so no notice is open when the buyer visits. Once you accept an offer, the title company runs a search, drafts the deed and sets the closing. At closing you sign, hand over keys and receive your proceeds once any mortgage and taxes are paid.

sections.h2: Preparing the house for showings or a buyer visit
sections.html: Even in an as-is sale, a little attention pays off. Clear the walkways, cut the grass, put away stored vehicles and remove brush piles so the lot does not draw a code notice while buyers are looking. Turn on the lights, open the blinds and make sure the buyer can reach the furnace, water heater and electrical panel. Keep receipts for any recent roof, furnace or plumbing work in one folder to hand over.

With cash there is no cleaning, no repair list and no staging, and no lender appraisal, which is the usual cause of closing delays. Title work, the deed and the last water bill still apply, so settle these early: the meter reading, any tax payoff and any clearance the county requires. Whoever you sell to, ask for the agreement in writing and read the closing costs line by line before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Inver Grove Heights house that has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the lease and the city rental license details. Because the city has been revising its rental licensing ordinance, ask the City Clerk what the license term and renewal rules are before you list.

faqs.q: How much notice does Inver Grove Heights utility billing need?
faqs.a: The city asks for at least one week of notice to schedule a water meter reading, and its number is 651-450-2520. Contact them before closing so the seller's final bill is accurate.

faqs.q: What is deed tax on an Inver Grove Heights sale?
faqs.a: The rate is 0.0033 of net consideration above $3,000, collected by Dakota County when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need a septic disclosure when selling in Inver Grove Heights?
faqs.a: Only if sewage on the property does not go to a permitted facility. Under Minnesota Statutes 115.55, you must then describe the system and map it before the purchase agreement is signed.

faqs.q: Are there special steps if the owner is on Medical Assistance?
faqs.a: Yes. Dakota County runs a certificates of clearance office at 651-554-6555. A call before you take an offer keeps that paperwork from delaying closing.
